script: I said "be nicer" to his mom, and the whole family turned on me.. I was at the fair, standing next to my boyfriend's mom, when she snapped at us again. She'd been shouting, blaming us for everything, and I was like, "If you want people to be more helpful, I suggest you work on being nicer." I didn't even think about the drama that would follow. I just felt annoyed and wanted to call her out on her attitude. (I know, right?) She didn't just shrug it off. She shoved my stuff, swore at me, and told my boyfriend's whole family that I was "mean, vindictive, and needed to grow the fuck up." Her sister even yelled about how "girlfriends should worship the ground their mothers walk on." It was like a live‑stream of humiliation, and I was the only one on the front row. (literally insane) My boyfriend said he agreed she was rude and that her reaction was bullying. He didn't say he was mad at me. He just wanted me to apologize, even though he never asked me to. He's not asking me to do it, but he thinks if I do, everyone can move on. The rest of his family kept pushing that same idea, saying I needed to be the adult and call her. They were all like, "She's going through a tough time—divorce, grief, deaths—so you need to fix this." (I know, right?) We're now in my hometown, visiting his grandma. She told me to call his mom, say I love her, and apologize. She said she was in a vulnerable period and that I should be the one to mend things. That hit me harder than a punch to the gut. I've survived childhood abuse, a traumatic miscarriage, my parents fighting cancer, and now I am pregnant with a non‑viable pregnancy. I am not about to be a martyr for anyone else's pain. (I know, right?) I am not completely refusing to reach out. I'd consider leaving a voicemail that says, "Hey Diane, I am thinking about you, I am sorry we had a rough time at the fair. I love you and I've been anxious about all this." It'd be sincere, but I am scared it'll be seen as me taking the blame for everything. The last time I apologized, she called me aggressive and rude. I don't want to be the one who keeps apologizing while the real hurt never gets acknowledged. (I know, right?) My boyfriend's stance is confusing. He says the family is right that I was disrespectful. He thinks I should open communication. But I am not sure if he's pushing me to do something that keeps the cycle alive. He's used to his family's dynamics and sees my discomfort as a personal flaw. He's never asked me to apologize for his mom, but he expects me to smooth things over. (I know, right?) I am not trying to leave him. The relationship is solid—compatible, loving, supportive. He's been my rock. But this whole family drama is making me question whether I can stay in a system that expects me to absorb disrespect and fix everything. It feels like I am the only one who has to make peace while everyone else stays rigid. So the question is: Am I the jerk for hesitating to call? Would a voicemail be a good olive branch or just another way for the family to say, "You're the problem." I am stuck between doing nothing and letting the house stay on fire, or apologizing and possibly making it worse. (I know, right?) I am stuck, bestie. I just want to know if I am the one who needs to fix this or if I am being set up to be the martyr.
